title: Homeostasis and Feedback in Body Systems Core Test
description: Use feedback models, data, and system interactions to explain how bodies keep cells working.

questions.prompt: A runner's heart rate rises during exercise and lowers during rest. What does this pattern show?
questions.questionText: A runner's heart rate rises during exercise and lowers during rest. What does this pattern show?
options: Body systems can adjust to changing cell needs.
The circulatory system disappears during rest.
Cells stop needing materials during exercise.
Heart rate is unrelated to activity.
questions.correctAnswer: Body systems can adjust to changing cell needs.
questions.explanation: Heart rate changes help deliver materials when cells need more energy.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best shows a feedback pathway for body temperature?
questions.questionText: Which sequence best shows a feedback pathway for body temperature?
options: stimulus -> receptors -> signals -> control center -> response
control center -> no signals -> no body change
questions.correctAnswer: stimulus -> receptors -> signals -> control center -> response
questions.explanation: Feedback uses detection, signaling, processing, and response.

questions.prompt: A person sweats on a hot day. Which function does sweating support?
questions.questionText: A person sweats on a hot day. Which function does sweating support?
questions.correctAnswer: helping cool the body
questions.explanation: Sweating helps remove heat as water evaporates from skin.

questions.prompt: Which body systems interact when breathing rate increases during exercise?
questions.questionText: Which body systems interact when breathing rate increases during exercise?
options: respiratory, circulatory, muscular, and nervous systems
questions.correctAnswer: respiratory, circulatory, muscular, and nervous systems
questions.explanation: Exercise responses involve several interacting systems.

questions.prompt: A student says, "The body responds randomly to changes." Which evidence best challenges that claim?
questions.questionText: A student says, "The body responds randomly to changes." Which evidence best challenges that claim?
options: Heart rate and breathing rate predictably rise during activity.
questions.correctAnswer: Heart rate and breathing rate predictably rise during activity.
questions.explanation: Predictable changes show coordinated responses.

questions.prompt: A model shows low water level in the body -> thirst -> drinking water. What does the model show?
questions.questionText: A model shows low water level in the body -> thirst -> drinking water. What does the model show?
options: a response that helps restore internal balance
questions.correctAnswer: a response that helps restore internal balance
questions.explanation: Thirst can help the body respond to low water levels.

questions.prompt: Which evidence supports that the nervous system helps regulate responses?
questions.questionText: Which evidence supports that the nervous system helps regulate responses?
options: The nervous system is always visible from outside.
Bones create nerve signals without cells.
Signals from receptors are processed before muscles or glands respond.
questions.correctAnswer: Signals from receptors are processed before muscles or glands respond.
questions.explanation: Receptors and signals help the body detect and respond to changes.

questions.prompt: A person shivers in cold air. Which explanation best connects systems and cells?
questions.questionText: A person shivers in cold air. Which explanation best connects systems and cells?
options: Muscle activity produces heat that helps maintain conditions for cells.
questions.correctAnswer: Muscle activity produces heat that helps maintain conditions for cells.
questions.explanation: Shivering uses muscles to produce heat.

questions.prompt: Which data would best show that the body responds to exercise?
questions.questionText: Which data would best show that the body responds to exercise?
options: pulse and breathing rate before, during, and after exercise
number of windows in the gym
questions.correctAnswer: pulse and breathing rate before, during, and after exercise
questions.explanation: Pulse and breathing rate track body responses to changing activity.

questions.prompt: A student writes: stimulus -> response -> receptor -> brain. What correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student writes: stimulus -> response -> receptor -> brain. What correction is best?
options: The response should happen before detection.
Receptors detect the stimulus before the response.
The brain is always first before any stimulus exists.
questions.correctAnswer: Receptors detect the stimulus before the response.
questions.explanation: Detection comes before processing and response.

questions.prompt: Why is feedback important for multicellular organisms?
questions.questionText: Why is feedback important for multicellular organisms?
options: It prevents cells from needing materials.
It makes every system work alone.
It helps keep internal conditions within workable ranges for cells.
It stops all responses to the environment.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps keep internal conditions within workable ranges for cells.
questions.explanation: Cells need stable internal conditions to function.

questions.prompt: A person smells smoke and leaves a room. Which part of the pathway is the stimulus?
questions.questionText: A person smells smoke and leaves a room. Which part of the pathway is the stimulus?
questions.correctAnswer: smoke chemicals in the air
questions.explanation: The stimulus is the environmental information detected by receptors.

questions.prompt: Which claim is supported when body temperature stays near 37 C in a warm and cool room?
questions.questionText: Which claim is supported when body temperature stays near 37 C in a warm and cool room?
options: The body can regulate internal temperature across different external conditions.
The room has no effect on the body.
Cells do not need stable conditions.
questions.correctAnswer: The body can regulate internal temperature across different external conditions.
questions.explanation: Maintaining similar internal temperature suggests regulation.

questions.prompt: A model leaves out blood flow during temperature regulation. What weakness does it have?
questions.questionText: A model leaves out blood flow during temperature regulation. What weakness does it have?
options: It misses one way heat can be moved around the body.
It proves blood is not involved in systems.
questions.correctAnswer: It misses one way heat can be moved around the body.
questions.explanation: Blood flow helps move heat and materials.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows a body response matching a stimulus?
questions.questionText: Which example best shows a body response matching a stimulus?
questions.correctAnswer: bright light -> pupils get smaller
questions.explanation: Pupil size can respond to light level.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Fast responses do not use the nervous system." Which evidence best corrects the idea?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Fast responses do not use the nervous system." Which evidence best corrects the idea?
options: The digestive system controls every fast response.
Receptors are used only in slow responses.
Some nervous-system pathways can trigger responses very quickly.
questions.correctAnswer: Some nervous-system pathways can trigger responses very quickly.
questions.explanation: Fast responses can still depend on nerves and receptors.

questions.prompt: Which question would best test whether sweating helps cooling?
questions.questionText: Which question would best test whether sweating helps cooling?
options: Does skin temperature change after sweating under controlled conditions?
Which day of the week is warmest?
Can the word sweat be spelled correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: Does skin temperature change after sweating under controlled conditions?
questions.explanation: A controlled measurement can test the cooling effect.

questions.prompt: A graph shows blood sugar rising after a meal and later returning toward normal. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: A graph shows blood sugar rising after a meal and later returning toward normal. Which claim is best supported?
options: Body systems help regulate internal nutrient levels.
questions.correctAnswer: Body systems help regulate internal nutrient levels.
questions.explanation: A rise and return pattern suggests regulation.

questions.prompt: Which model revision would improve: exercise -> tired?
questions.questionText: Which model revision would improve: exercise -> tired?
options: exercise -> muscle cell energy demand increases -> breathing and heart rate rise -> materials move faster
questions.correctAnswer: exercise -> muscle cell energy demand increases -> breathing and heart rate rise -> materials move faster
questions.explanation: The improved model explains intermediate system interactions.

questions.prompt: A person is dehydrated. Which response would most directly help restore water balance?
questions.questionText: A person is dehydrated. Which response would most directly help restore water balance?
questions.correctAnswer: feeling thirsty and drinking water
questions.explanation: Drinking water addresses low water level.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would weaken the claim that heart rate changes are unrelated to activity?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would weaken the claim that heart rate changes are unrelated to activity?
options: Repeated trials show heart rate rises during exercise and returns near resting after rest.
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated trials show heart rate rises during exercise and returns near resting after rest.
questions.explanation: A repeated pattern linked to activity weakens the claim.

questions.prompt: Why is one body system alone usually not enough to explain exercise?
questions.questionText: Why is one body system alone usually not enough to explain exercise?
options: Cells need oxygen, food molecules, signals, support, and waste removal from multiple systems.
questions.correctAnswer: Cells need oxygen, food molecules, signals, support, and waste removal from multiple systems.
questions.explanation: Exercise requires several systems interacting to support cells.

questions.prompt: A student claims feedback always makes a condition increase. What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student claims feedback always makes a condition increase. What is the best correction?
options: Some feedback responses reduce a change and help restore balance.
questions.correctAnswer: Some feedback responses reduce a change and help restore balance.
questions.explanation: Many regulation responses counteract a change.

questions.prompt: Which scenario best shows regulation rather than random change?
questions.questionText: Which scenario best shows regulation rather than random change?
options: a notebook falls off a table
a label is moved to another desk
breathing rate increases when carbon dioxide rises during activity
questions.correctAnswer: breathing rate increases when carbon dioxide rises during activity
questions.explanation: The response matches an internal condition created by activity.

questions.prompt: A model includes stimulus and response but not receptors. What key idea is missing?
questions.questionText: A model includes stimulus and response but not receptors. What key idea is missing?
options: how the body detects the change
questions.correctAnswer: how the body detects the change
questions.explanation: Receptors detect stimuli and start information flow.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best connects feedback to homeostasis?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best connects feedback to homeostasis?
options: Feedback uses information and responses to keep internal conditions in a workable range.
Feedback removes the need for cells.
questions.correctAnswer: Feedback uses information and responses to keep internal conditions in a workable range.
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is maintaining workable internal conditions.

questions.prompt: A person moves from shade into strong sunlight. Which response is most directly related to light detection?
questions.questionText: A person moves from shade into strong sunlight. Which response is most directly related to light detection?
options: stomach digests faster because light is loud
pupils get smaller after eye receptors detect bright light
questions.correctAnswer: pupils get smaller after eye receptors detect bright light
questions.explanation: Eye receptors detect light, and pupil size can respond.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern best supports a feedback explanation?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern best supports a feedback explanation?
options: Only one unrelated number is recorded.
A variable moves away from normal, a response occurs, and the variable moves back toward normal.
questions.correctAnswer: A variable moves away from normal, a response occurs, and the variable moves back toward normal.
questions.explanation: Feedback often shows a change followed by a response and partial return.

questions.prompt: Which final explanation best shows understanding of body feedback?
questions.questionText: Which final explanation best shows understanding of body feedback?
options: Body systems use receptors, signals, and responses to adjust conditions so cells can keep working.
Cells do not depend on internal conditions.
Receptors act after responses are finished.
questions.correctAnswer: Body systems use receptors, signals, and responses to adjust conditions so cells can keep working.
questions.explanation: This connects feedback pathways, body systems, and cell needs.

questions.prompt: Which question pushes beyond memorizing the pathway?
questions.questionText: Which question pushes beyond memorizing the pathway?
options: How many letters are in receptor?
What would happen to the response if the receptor could not detect the stimulus?
questions.correctAnswer: What would happen to the response if the receptor could not detect the stimulus?
questions.explanation: Changing one part of the model tests understanding of the system.
